why.rules.encyclopedia: 3.7–3.8 (owner: are these all real facts? check everything, replace what is wrong). Every one of the 99 statements was checked together with its number against sources (docs/facts-review.md, docs/analytics/data/facts_check.json). 3.7 left 21 of them out of the game; 3.8 puts a correct statement in the place of each and rewords five more, so all 99 are in the game again and `excluded` is empty. A new fact in place of a false or unverifiable one: 11 the Great Pyramid, 12 the Statue of Liberty, 18 the centre of the Sun, 33 tungsten, 39 hairs on a head, 41 seconds in a day, 45 mercury, 66 the Ampex videotape recorder, 73 Neptune, 76 the keys of a piano, 79 the Île Vierge lighthouse, 85 the first published ketchup recipe, 88 Rubik's cube, 89 Drais, 94 the World Wide Web. The record that holds today: 9 the Statue of Unity, 71 the Gotthard Base Tunnel. The same fact stated correctly: 8, 10, 25, 27, 34, 59, 60, 87, 90. Numbers brought up to date: 13 Mammoth Cave 686 km, 20 gold, 28 the Nile, 29 silver, 30 platinum (3.8); 19, 35, 36, 44, 68 (3.7); 12, 13, 16, 17, 21, 24, 26, 27, 56, 58, 92 (3.2–3.3). A statement is the key of its translations, so a reworded one has a new `name` with new texts in all 14 languages; slips in the English of the kept ones are corrected in data/locales/en.json, the keys stay. No two statements share a number (the options of a question are the numbers of other statements). Records to look at again when they change: 9, 13, 71.

why.iv_show_results.i2_points_arr: The value stays (a wrong answer costs 0, applied in 3.2.0), the reason is restated for the new levels. With -p per wrong answer the score is p x (right - wrong): every step would need a perfect game and a game with half of the answers wrong would score 0, so ordinary games of the average player would count as weak (29 % on medium and 47 % on hard in the round-1 model). There is no way to skip a question, so the penalty changes only the scale, never the play. With 0 the score is p x right answers and each threshold reads as 'so many right': 3 of 4 on easy, 4 of 5 on medium, 6 of 7 on hard; weak games of the average player 1 % on medium and 3 % on hard.
why.MG_interesting_values_hard.level_up_para: up 18000 = 6 of the 7 answers right (3000 each): novice 2 %, average 24 %, strong 80 %; weak games (< 7200 = two right answers or fewer): average 3 %, novice 29 %. 41 games for the 10 steps of the average player, 12 of the strong one. Mean scores of the average player rise 5653 / 9388 / 14030 (x1.66, x1.49); there is no time or mistake penalty in this game.
why.iv_lev_0.m_nPages: Content ladder: every level showed the same 8 facts (4 pages x 2); only the questions (3 / 4 / 5) and the page time (30 / 25 / 20 s) changed, and in the memory model (tools/analysis/train_balance_encyclopedia.mjs: a player holds K facts of a session, K = 3.1 / 5.7 / 8.6 solved from the doc's 50 / 75 / 95 % right answers) the share of right answers was the same on all three levels. Easy now shows 6 facts (3 pages): right answers 57 / 86 / 96 % (novice / average / strong).
why.iv_lev_0.m_nTargetsCount: 3.6 targets (docs/analytics/medium-levels.md: easy — novice 60–75 % of games, average ≥ 95 %): Easy asks 5 of the 6 facts and allows two misses (up 4950 = 3 of 5 right). With 4 questions and one miss (3.3) the novice passed 42 % of the games; two misses of 4 would pass 81 % (and a player who only guesses among the four options, 26 %). 3 of 5: novice 66 %, average 98 %, strong 100 %, guessing 10 %. Mean score of the average player 7074 (Medium 9376, Hard 14005).
why.iv_lev_1.m_nTargetsCount: Medium keeps 8 facts and 25 s a page and asks 5 of them with one miss allowed (up = 4 of 5) instead of 4 questions with none: average 30 % -> 64 %, novice 5 % -> 16 %, strong 76 % -> 97 %. Four questions with one miss would pass 74 % of the average player's games, four with none 30 %.
why.iv_lev_2.m_nPages: Hard shows 10 facts (5 pages x 2, 20 s a page) instead of the same 8: more than the average player holds (5.7), so the share of right answers falls to 46 / 67 / 88 % — the level is harder by its content, not by a stricter count of mistakes.
why.iv_lev_2.m_nTargetsCount: Hard asks 7 of the 10 facts and allows one miss (up = 6 of 7) instead of 5 questions with none: novice 2 %, average 24 %, strong 80 % — all three in the owner's bands (before, 5 of 5 on 8 facts: 2 / 20 / 61 %). Six questions with one miss would give 5 / 33 / 85 %.
why.MG_interesting_values_easy.level_up_para: 3.6 targets (docs/analytics/medium-levels.md: easy — novice 60–75 % of games, average ≥ 95 %): up stays 4950, now 3 of the 5 answers right (1650 each; wrong answers cost 0; see iv_lev_0.m_nTargetsCount): novice 42 → 66 %, average 91 → 98 %, strong 100 %. 3 games for the 3 steps of the average player, 4 of the novice (was 6). Unlock (4th number): level-ups needed to open the game. v3.3 (owner: the last games opened too slowly): 1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13, 15 instead of 1, 2, 3, 6, 8, 11, 14, 16, 18; with the 3.6 thresholds the average model player opens all 12 games in 17–23 trainings and the novice in 31–41 (was 23–30 and 63–86; tools/analysis/unlock_pace.py).
why.MG_interesting_values_med.level_up_param: 3.6 targets (docs/analytics/medium-levels.md: medium — novice 35–45 % of games, average ≥ 85 %): up 10000 → 7500 = 3 of the 5 answers right (2500 each; was 4 of 5): novice 16 → 50 %, average 64 → 91 %, strong 100 %; weak games (< 3000 = one right answer or none): average 1 %, novice 16 %. 5 games for the 5 steps of the average player (was 8), 10 of the novice (was 29). The scores step by 2500, so there is nothing between 4 of 5 (too strict) and 3 of 5.
